diff2ai.text: App imports are not wrapped in thunks, causing all 29 app packages to load eagerly when @calcom/app-store is imported instead of loading lazily as intended
Each app package being split into its own async chunk adds bundling overhead
If any app module fails to load, the rejected promise sits in the map as an unhandled rejection, which can crash Node processes even when the failing app is never used
Using forEach with async callbacks causes errors to escape the try/catch block, resulting in unhandled rejections from getCalendar, deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting calls

Using forEach with async callbacks means nothing waits for calendar and video deletions to complete before the handler continues with emails, DB updates, and response, causing race conditions and silently dropped failures

getCalendarCredentials now returns a Promise in the calendar field, which will break other callers that check if (calendar) or call calendar.method() since they will see a truthy Promise instead of the actual calendar object
Calendar promises in getCalendarCredentials are created eagerly, so if one rejects and is never awaited it becomes an unhandled rejection

Backup code consumption is not atomic - two concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed because both read the same stored ciphertext before either writes, allowing a single-use code to be used twice
Backup code lookup uses indexOf on secrets which is not a constant-time comparison, creating a timing side-channel vulnerability
Download button inside the form lacks e.preventDefault() and likely submits the TOTP form again when clicked, potentially causing spurious errors or unintended requests
Putting a <button> inside an <a> is invalid interactive nesting and hurts accessibility
Dismissing the dialog on the backup codes step via Escape or clicking overlay skips onEnable() and resetState(), leaving the parent unaware 2FA was enabled and causing stale state on reopen
resetState does not clear backupCodes or backupCodesUrl, leaving plaintext codes in component state after the flow ends
Blob URL for backup codes is never revoked on close or unmount, causing a memory leak
Disable endpoint returns 500 instead of 400 for a non-string backupCode because replaceAll assumes the value is a string
When all backup codes have been used (array holds only nulls), users see 'incorrect backup code' instead of the MissingBackupCodes message
Copy shows success toast without waiting for navigator.clipboard.writeText promise, so failures become unhandled rejections while user believes codes were copied
BackupCode component is exported as TwoFactor, duplicating the name of the real TwoFactor component and causing confusion in stack traces and React DevTools
No tests exist for backup code login, rejecting already-used codes, or disabling 2FA with a backup code
Download content and clipboard content are not tested
mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or [], causing TypeError crash when location is Google Meet instead of falling back to Cal Video

Organization creation slug condition is inverted - slug is now set when billing is enabled instead of disabled, causing slug assignment before payment/verification and missing slugs when billing is disabled

Google calendar update/delete fallback branch compares against falsy externalCalendarId, causing update to send undefined calendarId and delete to target primary instead of correct calendar for legacy references

Google createEvent ignores destination calendars without credentialId - legacy records with null credentialId are not matched, causing events to be created in primary instead of user's chosen calendar
Office365, CalDAV and Lark calendar providers always use destinationCalendar[0] (main host's calendar) for every host's credential, causing 404 errors or wrong calendar for non-main hosts
Team hosts' calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar because push on null silently does nothing
Video/conferencing references lose their credentialId - non-calendar results now get undefined credentialId, breaking later update/delete paths that look up video credential by reference.credentialId
Dynamic users query no longer selects organization slug, causing undefined for organizerUser.organization?.slug in dynamic group bookings
Dynamic users error handling changed - empty dynamicUserList becomes generic 500 and HttpError is rewritten to 400
Recurring cancellation is inside per-reference loop, causing same events to be deleted N times and other hosts' events in recurring bookings to never be deleted
updateEvent may be called with undefined credential if not found in calendarCredentials or DB, and credential declared outside loop may leak between iterations
Logging of calendar update failures was removed, causing failures to be swallowed silently

Returned SQL fragments are not wrapped in parentheses, causing top-level OR to bleed into caller predicates when combined with AND, potentially returning data outside requested filters and causing authorization leaks

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making the else if (filterConditions) branch and final NOTHING_CONDITION branch dead code that misleadingly suggests filter conditions alone could act as base condition
Public findMany method removed without visible migration of callers - replaced by getBaseConditions which returns raw SQL instead of rows, breaking any existing callers like tRPC insights routers
Caching tests deleted without replacement while caching logic (cachedAuthConditions and cachedFilterConditions) still exists and is no longer covered by any test

Loosened constructor type InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional for every scope, allowing invalid combinations like { scope: 'team' } without teamId to type-check, making misuse hard to diagnose
One failed SendGrid cancel blocks all later cancellations - if any client.request throws, the loop stops, remaining reminders are never cancelled, and deletes queued so far are never awaited
Query uses lte: now + 1h with no lower bound, matching reminders whose send time has already passed, and cancelling already-sent or invalid batch_id can fail at SendGrid
Failing rows are never deleted, so they are picked up again on every cron run and fail repeatedly, blocking all reminders after the bad one from being cancelled
SendGrid requests are awaited one at a time, making the cron slower as the backlog grows
immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but never removes the WorkflowReminder DB row
DELETE /v3/user/scheduled_sends/{id} call was removed, so cancelled batches pile up on the SendGrid account
Reminder cancellation is now fire-and-forget with unawaited promises - deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside forEach without awaiting
On serverless environments, the function can be frozen once response is sent, causing cancelled update, row delete, or Twilio/SendGrid cancel to never run
try/catch in handleNewBooking cannot catch rejections from unawaited promises
Ownership scope dropped from reminder deletion - old code used where: { id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id } } but new helpers delete/update by id only

Type-only imports (PrismaPromise, Prisma, App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput) converted to value imports, which may be unused and can cause lint/build errors under isolatedModules or verbatimModuleSyntax settings

Skip of the busy-time check on days with a date override - when a slot falls on a day that has a date override and inside its range, the function returns true straight away and the busy.every(...) check never runs, causing existing bookings and busy events from external calendars to be ignored and allowing double-booking

Slots rejected on days with more than one override or working-hours range - both checks use find which rejects the slot as soon as any single range on that day does not contain it, but a day can have several ranges and a slot should only be rejected when outside every range for that day

Unavailable all day check compares Dayjs objects by reference - dayjs(a) === dayjs(b) compares two newly created objects so it is always false, meaning a full-day-off override is never detected and slots starting exactly at the override start are still offered

Slot end time ignored in the override and working-hours checks - in the working-hours check end is computed from slotStartTime not slotEndTime, and the override check tests slotStartTime.isAfter(date.end), so slots that start inside but run past the end are incorrectly accepted

Override day matched by UTC calendar date not the organizer's local date - the override start is converted to real UTC and only its UTC date is compared with the slot's UTC date, but for organizers far from UTC one local day spans two UTC dates causing slots to be offered or blocked incorrectly

Override shifted to the invitee time zone can wrap past midnight - when the shift crosses midnight startTime becomes greater than endTime giving an invalid range and losing or misplacing the override's slots
When override.timeZone is undefined, dayjs(...).tz(undefined) falls back to the default or server time zone which can produce a wrong offset
dayjs(override.start.toString()) parses the non-ISO Date.toString() output which is fragile - should use dayjs(override.start) instead

Salesforce refreshes token on every getClient call with no expiry check, hitting token endpoint and writing to DB unnecessarily
Salesforce bypasses refreshOAuthTokens so sync endpoint is never used, but uses minimal schema when sync enabled which strips instance_url
Salesforce uses response.statusText !== 'OK' which is unreliable since HTTP/2 responses have empty statusText - should use response.ok
Salesforce lines 92-94 are dead code because parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure
HttpError may not be imported in the Salesforce diff
Webhook secret compared with non-constant-time equality (!==) which leaks timing information
Webhook secret header value can be string[] but is not handled

Invalid body from schema.parse throws unhandled exception producing 500 instead of 400
symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse failures throw unhandled exceptions producing 500 instead of 400 and may leak error messages

parsedToken.success checks in Zoom and Office365 are dead code since parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on failure

Retry-count cleanup deletes reminders of every method, not just SMS - the new OR branch { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } has no method filter, so the SMS cron job will delete any WorkflowReminder whose retryCount > 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders

Unguarded DB update in catch block can abort the whole batch - prisma.workflowReminder.update inside catch is not protected and can throw (P2025 if reminder was deleted concurrently, or on DB connectivity error), causing remaining reminders to go unprocessed and returning a 500

Reminders already scheduled with Twilio can be counted as failures and deleted - if twilio.scheduleSMS succeeds but the later update that sets scheduled: true and referenceId throws, the reminder is counted as failed and retryCount is incremented, leading to duplicate messages and lost referenceId

Non-atomic increment of retryCount - retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 is a read-modify-write on a stale value, so if two cron invocations overlap, increments are lost; should use Prisma's { increment: 1 } instead
Duplicated retry threshold logic with magic number - the cutoff gt: 1 is a magic number allowing only two failed attempts before silent deletion, and the update logic is duplicated in two places

isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring users to be both admin AND owner, so team admins get FORBIDDEN error when they should be allowed
